title: The Riemann existence theorem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: For every scheme X locally of finite type over the complex numbers, finite etale covers of X are the same as finite covering spaces of X(C), without any normality hypothesis: the classical topology and finite etale morphisms as covering maps, connected components and full faithfulness, finite covers of punctured polydiscs and their extension by locally bounded functions, the smooth case by snc compactification and GAGA, descent of finite etale covers along proper surjective morphisms, the general theorem by descent along the resolution, its analytic form, and the comparison of the etale and topological fundamental groups.
prerequisites: AG-QC lessons on complex analytic spaces and analytification and on Serre's comparison theorems (GAGA)
Complex analytic spaces and coherent sheaves, lesson 1 (Riemann extension theorem)
Resolution of singularities in characteristic zero (Theorem 4.8, Corollary 5.2)
Core course D60 Algebraic Topology (path lifting, monodromy, Theorem 10.1, Corollary 12.1, Theorem 17.1)
AI Integrated Stacks Project: finite etale morphisms, henselian rings, fpqc descent, Galois categories
Subanalytic triangulations on analytic manifolds: relative polyhedron theorem and its stated subanalytic prerequisites (Proposition 3.3)
free_sources: Grothendieck et al., SGA 1, arXiv:math/0206203 (Expose XII sections 1-5, Expose IX sections 3-4, Expose V)
Serre, GAGA, Ann. Inst. Fourier 6 (1956), Numdam
Lojasiewicz, Triangulation of semi-analytic sets, Ann. SNS Pisa 18 (1964), Numdam (triangulation context)
open_items: Proposition 3.3 supplies local contractibility from the relative polyhedron theorem. The subanalytic prerequisites explicitly used by that theorem remain separate dependencies; this course does not certify their full recursive closure.
